name: Kodak Professional T400 CN (Process C-41)
notes: The sheet carries a notice that the film has been discontinued, recommending Kodak Professional BW400CN.

Chromogenic black-and-white film (C-41). The sheet plots THREE characteristic curves, B, G and R, in Status M (like a colour negative: base levels about 0.45 / 0.40 / 0.21 at the toe), not one neutral curve; they are traced as curves/b, curves/g, curves/r and there is no curves/v, so the sheet is not buildable as 'bw-negative' without choosing or deriving a neutral curve.

Characteristic curves: x axis is absolute log exposure in lux-seconds (daylight), Log H Reference -1.44 printed on the plot. This plot has tick labels only for -3.0, -2.0, -1.0, 0.0 (calibrated on the tick marks); the curves run from about -3.43 to 0.57, the frame edges.

Spectral sensitivity: one curve, daylight, effective exposure 1/100 s, process C-41, Status M, density 0.2 above D-min; sensitivity/v. Log sensitivity = reciprocal of exposure (ergs/cm2) as printed. The curve starts at 400 nm and ends near 650 nm.

Spectral dye density: dyes/mid is 'Midscale Neutral' (typical densities for a midscale neutral subject) and dyes/min 'Minimum Density' (D-min), process C-41, diffuse spectral density, 400 to 700 nm. Both start at the left edge (400 nm) at a high value (about 2.3 and 1.55) and fall steeply in the first few nm.

Grain: RMS granularity 9 ('extremely fine'), read at a net diffuse visual density of 1.00 with a 48 micrometre aperture. Speed EI 400 with a stated latitude of EI 25 to 1600 (+4 stops / -2 stops from EI 400).
